He helped establish and improve a multi-level urban housing supply system with economically affordable housing as the main component. He also promoted the establishment of the basic framework for a socialist market economy, oversaw the completion of the {{17}} negotiations for China's accession to the World Trade Organization, and advanced the country's opening up in both scope and depth. Zhu had deep affection for the people.
paragraphs.cn: 他强调，要千方百计促进下岗职工再就业，加强社会保障体系建设。他推进住房制度改革，逐步以货币化住房补贴取代实物分房。他帮助建立和完善以经济适用住房为主的多层次城镇住房供应体系。他还推动建立社会主义市场经济体制的基本框架，完成了中国加入世界贸易组织的艰苦谈判，推动对外开放向广度和深度拓展。朱镕基对人民怀有深厚的感情。

He stressed the need to take the initiative, with a strong sense of responsibility, to shoulder heavy burdens, take on tough problems and go all out to deliver real results for the people, it added. In March 2003, Zhu no longer served as premier of the State Council. After retiring from leadership posts, he {{18}} upheld and supported the CPC Central Committee with Hu Jintao as general secretary, and then the CPC Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core. He continued to care about the great cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics and firmly supported efforts to improve conduct, promote integrity and fight corruption.

articles.fullText:
A file photo of former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji, who died of illness at the age of 98 in Beijing at 11:06 a.m. Wednesday. /Xinhua
Former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji died of illness at the age of 98 in Beijing at 11:06 a.m. on Wednesday.
Zhu had served as a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the 14th and 15th Central Committees of the Communist Party of China (CPC).
An obituary, jointly issued by the CPC Central Committee, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the State Council and the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, extolled Zhu as an excellent Party member, a time-tested and loyal communist fighter, and an outstanding proletarian revolutionist, statesman and leader of the Party and the state.
Zhu was born in October 1928 in Changsha, central China's Hunan Province. He studied in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Tsinghua University from 1947 to 1951. He joined the CPC in October 1949.
From 1951 to 1983, Zhu worked at various places and held a series of posts related to economic affairs in regional and central government departments and institutions. He served as deputy director of the now-defunct State Economic Commission from 1983 to 1987.
Between 1987 and 1991, he served successively as deputy secretary of the CPC Shanghai Municipal Committee, mayor of Shanghai, and secretary of the CPC Shanghai Municipal Committee.
In Shanghai, he urged the municipality to readjust its industrial structure, cultivate new development strengths, enhance its international competitiveness, and pursue an export-oriented development path.
In 1991, Zhu was appointed vice premier of the State Council.
In October 1992, Zhu was elected a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and its standing committee, and took charge of the State Council's day-to-day work.
In June 1993, he concurrently served as the governor of the People's Bank of China.
He actively championed the implementation of the principles outlined in Deng Xiaoping's remarks during Deng's 1992 southern China tour and worked hard to promote reform and opening up as well as China's modernization drive.
He organized campaigns to resolve the problem of debt chains known as the "triangular debts."
Also, he studied and developed approaches and measures to strengthen and improve macroeconomic regulation, making significant and effective contributions to curbing an overheated economy, reining in inflation and achieving an economic "soft landing."
He pushed forward efforts to rectify and restore order in the fiscal and taxation sectors, accelerated fiscal and tax reforms and helped improve China's financial regulation system.
In September 1997, Zhu was re-elected a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and its standing committee.
In March 1998, Zhu was appointed premier of the State Council. Facing the impact of the Asian financial crisis and the catastrophic flooding in China, he implemented the plans of the Party Central Committee to shift from a moderately tight fiscal and monetary policy to a proactive fiscal policy and a prudent monetary policy, expand domestic demand and deepen reforms in key areas, thereby sustaining steady and rapid economic growth.
He introduced a series of policies and measures to broaden opening up and encourage exports, while firmly preventing the devaluation of the renminbi. He also took measures to actively attract foreign investment and better utilize both domestic and international markets and resources, and firmly safeguarded the prosperity and stability of Hong Kong as an international financial center.
Zhu worked to establish the basic living security system for laid-off workers from state-owned enterprises, the unemployment insurance system, and the minimum living guarantee system for urban residents. He also made great efforts to address issues such as wage arrears and the re-employment of laid-off workers.
During Zhu's tenure as vice premier and premier of the State Council, China was in a critical period of transitioning from a planned economy to a socialist market economy.
Under the firm leadership of the CPC Central Committee with Jiang Zemin at the core, Zhu spearheaded reform of the fiscal and taxation systems, carrying out a major overhaul of the tax regime centered on fairer tax burdens and a simplified tax system. He introduced a tax sharing system based on a rational division of fiscal responsibilities between the central and local governments, and launched pilot reforms of taxes and fees in rural areas. He actively promoted the reform of the financial system, further regulated the functions of the central bank, deepened reforms of commercial banks, the foreign exchange system, and the securities and futures markets, and promoted the establishment of a nationally unified and open financial market system with orderly competition and strict regulation.
Zhu took the reform of state-owned enterprises as the central link of economic structural reform. He stressed that every effort must be made to promote the re-employment of laid-off workers and strengthen the social security system.
He advanced housing reform, gradually replacing the allocation of housing to employees with monetary housing benefits. He helped establish and improve a multi-level urban housing supply system with economically affordable housing as the main component.
He also promoted the establishment of the basic framework for a socialist market economy, oversaw the completion of the arduous negotiations for China's accession to the World Trade Organization, and advanced the country's opening up in both scope and depth.
Zhu had deep affection for the people. He emphasized that government officials must always bear in mind that they are public servants and should have the courage to speak the truth, not fear giving offense, and refrain from seeking special privileges, the obituary said.
He stressed the need to take the initiative, with a strong sense of responsibility, to shoulder heavy burdens, take on tough problems and go all out to deliver real results for the people, it added.
In March 2003, Zhu no longer served as premier of the State Council.
After retiring from leadership posts, he steadfastly upheld and supported the CPC Central Committee with Hu Jintao as general secretary, and then the CPC Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core. He continued to care about the great cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics and firmly supported efforts to improve conduct, promote integrity and fight corruption.
Zhu's life was a revolutionary, fighting and glorious one. His death is a great loss to the Party and the state, the obituary said.

paragraphs.en: Editor's note: Qin Mengyao is an editor and podcast producer whose work focuses on Chinese culture, youth and social trends. This year's International Youth Day theme, "Different Contexts, Common Aspirations," highlights a powerful truth: despite wildly different national realities, young people everywhere share similar hopes for dignity, opportunity and a sustainable future. One of the most {{1}} places to observe this is China, where rapid societal shifts have created a unique arena for the younger generation, one filled with both challenges and possibilities for reinvention. To understand how this global pursuit is {{2}} in the world's second-largest economy, one of the most {{3}} places to look is the digital realm. Across Chinese social media, a highly specific vocabulary has taken root.
paragraphs.cn: 编者按：秦梦瑶是一位编辑和播客制作人，其工作聚焦于中国文化、青年和社会趋势。今年国际青年日的主题“不同背景，共同愿望”揭示了一个有力的真相：尽管各国现实截然不同，但世界各地的年轻人对尊严、机会和可持续未来抱有相似的期望。观察这一现象最引人注目的地方之一是中国，那里快速的社会变迁为年轻一代创造了一个独特的舞台，既充满挑战，也充满重塑自我的可能性。要理解这一全球追求如何在全球第二大经济体中体现，最值得关注的地方之一是数字领域。在中国的社交媒体上，一套高度特定的词汇已经扎根。

This year's International Youth Day theme, "Different Contexts, Common Aspirations," highlights a powerful truth: despite wildly different national realities, young people everywhere share similar hopes for dignity, opportunity and a sustainable future.
One of the most compelling places to observe this is China, where rapid societal shifts have created a unique arena for the younger generation, one filled with both challenges and possibilities for reinvention. To understand how this global pursuit is manifesting in the world's second-largest economy, one of the most revealing places to look is the digital realm.
Across Chinese social media, a highly specific vocabulary has taken root. Words like qumei (祛魅) – disenchantment – and huorengan (活人感) – the feeling of genuine humanity – are far more than fleeting internet slang. From a cultural perspective, they represent a profound generational shift. Rather than outright rejection of the highly structured world they inherited, Chinese youngsters are using this new language to question old orthodoxies, redefining the parameters of a meaningful life on their own terms.

The end of blind reverence
Perhaps no word better captures this shift than qumei. The term describes a willingness to look beyond the aura surrounding things once considered unquestionably desirable, from prestigious careers and elite institutions to social status and symbolic success. It does not mean rejecting expertise or ambition, but refusing to confuse prestige with true value.
This same desire to let go of traditional expectations has driven the rise of ling fuzhai qingnian (零负债青年) – zero-debt youth. It represents a deep-seated urge to reduce unnecessary burdens, whether financial, emotional or social, freeing young people from the crushing weight of traditional adult milestones.

Rebuilding everyday meaning
Beyond chasing traditional milestones of success, many young people are asking a more fundamental question: how should life be experienced?
Renlei fengrong (人类丰容) – human enrichment – offers one answer. It encourages people to explore niche interests and create moments of curiosity simply for the joy of the experience itself.
Meanwhile, huorengan reflects a search for authenticity in an increasingly polished digital world. As AI-generated content and filtered realities become seamless and ubiquitous, imperfections – spontaneous reactions, emotional warmth and small, relatable flaws – have gained premium value.
Young readers spend a summer day at a library in Tongling, Anhui Province, August 4, 2026. /CFP
Pragmatism over orthodoxy
When it comes to navigating the actual challenges of this new reality, another buzzword, xiexiu (邪修) – unorthodox cultivation – reveals how young people navigate uncertainty. Originally a term from martial arts fiction describing unconventional training techniques, it has been repurposed online as a humorous celebration of creative problem-solving. It describes solutions that seem strange at first glance – but somehow work.
Behind the humor is a highly pragmatic attitude: effectiveness over convention. It is an acknowledgment that societal rules are merely tools to be utilized, not absolute truths to be blindly followed.
Together, these expressions reveal a broader shift: fulfillment is no longer strictly about maximizing achievement, but about curating the conditions for a sustainable, meaningful life. Success and ambition still matter, but they are increasingly viewed as tools for living well rather than the final destination.

Taken individually, these expressions may look like playful internet trends. But taken together, they breathe life into the core message of International Youth Day. While Chinese youth are navigating their own unique social and economic realities – their "different contexts" – they share a "common aspiration" with their global peers: a resolute desire to live with greater authenticity, flexibility and self-direction.
Language does not merely reflect social change; it helps people understand it. Each new buzzword gives shape to an emerging reality, allowing a generation to narrate its own story. Ultimately, the story these expressions tell transcends internet culture.

The first Hualong One nuclear power unit in south China's Hainan Province was connected to the power grid on Saturday, marking a key milestone before the reactor enters commercial operation.
The unit, officially Unit 3 of the Phase II Changjiang Nuclear Power Plant, uses China's domestically developed third-generation Hualong One nuclear reactor technology. Following grid connection, the unit will undergo a series of commissioning, efficiency optimization and performance tests before being put into full commercial service.
The second phase of the Changjiang project consists of two 1.2-gigawatt nuclear power units. Once both reactors are operational, they are expected to generate about 18 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity annually, according to He Qingwei, a senior operator at the Changjiang Nuclear Power Plant.
The project is expected to save around 6.3 million tonnes of standard coal each year while reducing carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 11.6 million tonnes, contributing to energy security and China's climate goals, He said.
China has pledged to peak carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060.
Multiple innovations
The Hualong One reactor incorporates several safety features developed with independent Chinese intellectual property.
One of its most notable designs is a double containment structure. Unlike earlier-generation reactors that used a single containment shell, this Hualong One features both an inner and an outer protective barrier.
The inner containment consists of 1.3 meters of reinforced concrete lined with a 6-millimeter steel plate, designed to securely contain radioactive materials. The outer containment is built with 1.8 meters of high-strength concrete, providing additional protection against external impacts.
The reactor island contains approximately 230,000 tonnes of reinforcing steel, and the containment structure is designed to withstand the impact of extremely heavy external forces.
Another key safety feature is its passive emergency cooling system. A gravity-fed water tank capable of storing about 2,400 tonnes of water can automatically inject cooling water into the reactor without external electricity or human intervention if an emergency occurs. The system can continue cooling the reactor for up to 72 hours, helping maintain safe temperatures and providing operators with valuable time to respond.

Zambians vote on Thursday, August 13, in a closely watched presidential election. Up to 8.7 million registered voters will decide whether President Hakainde Hichilema's economic reforms deserve another term or whether the opposition can turn widespread discontent into a comeback.
Although 14 candidates are on the ballot, analysts say the race has narrowed into a two-horse contest between Hichilema and Brian Mundubile, a 55-year-old former minister and lawyer.
(FILES) Zambia's presidential candidate for the opposition, Hakainde Hichilema (R) of the United Party for National Development (UPND) casts his ballot in Lusaka on August 12, 2021.
Here is a look at the leading hopefuls:
Hakainde Hichilema
Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema, 64, won the presidency in 2021 on his sixth attempt, defeating then-President Edgar Lungu by a wide margin after years as the country's main opposition leader. He won 59.02% of the vote.
His victory came as Zambia was grappling with a severe debt crisis and economic difficulties. His government has since overseen debt restructuring and an improvement in key economic indicators, although many households continue to struggle with the cost of living.
On the campaign trail, he embraced the youth catchphrase "Salt Sana" — or "more salt" — urging voters to "add more flavour" by re-electing him for a second and final five-year term.
Brian Mundubile
Brian Mundubile, 55, a lawyer and former minister, has emerged as Hichilema's main opposition challenger after being selected as the presidential candidate of the Tonse Alliance. The alliance later merged with the PF-Pamodzi Alliance, with constitutional lawyer Makebi Zulu as Mundubile's running mate.
Mundubile served as Northern Province minister and later as government chief whip under Lungu's Patriotic Front administration. His campaign has drawn on the political legacy of the late former president while portraying the opposition alliance as a vehicle for change.
He has focused heavily on the cost of living and persistent poverty, arguing that improvements in economic indicators have not translated into sufficient relief for ordinary Zambians.
Harry Kalaba
Former Foreign Affairs Minister Harry Kalaba, 50, is seeking the presidency for a second time as leader of the Citizens First party. Kalaba left Lungu's government in 2019 and later contested the 2021 presidential election, finishing third with 25,231 votes, or 0.52% of the total.
He has returned to the race promising a stronger performance and is campaigning as an alternative opposition voice, although his campaign has been overshadowed by Mundubile's growing profile.

七局四胜的决赛开局迅速，KSG拿下首局。AG.AL在第二局以微弱优势获胜，将比分扳平，但KSG迅速调整策略，赢下第三局重新取得领先。随后AG.AL找到节奏，连续赢下接下来两局，以3-2领先，距离冠军仅一步之遥。面临淘汰的KSG在第六局以针对性的进攻有效限制了AG.AL的攻势，顽强反击。AG.AL在后期发起冲击试图扭转局面，但KSG顶住压力，将比赛拖入决胜局。

2026电竞世界杯于7月6日在巴黎开幕，将持续至8月23日。今年的电竞世界杯是首届在沙特阿拉伯利雅得以外举办。本届赛事汇聚了来自100多个国家和地区的2000多名职业选手和200多家俱乐部，参加25项锦标赛和24款游戏的角逐，总奖金池超过7500万美元，创下纪录。（封面：快手游戏（KSG）于2026年8月8日在法国巴黎电竞世界杯上赢得王者荣耀世界杯冠军。/电竞世界杯）
